definition: Bilingual education is an educational setting in which children learn and communicate in two languages, typically their first language and a second language. In this context, development in the second language, including pronunciation, can affect how effectively children communicate.

reasons: The packet discusses children’s bilingual education and second-language pronunciation in communicative contexts, but it does not support a general dictionary definition of bilingual education as an educational setting where children learn and communicate in two languages.

The phrase “typically their first language and a second language” is not established by the packet as a defining feature of bilingual education; the packet focuses on L1/L2 pronunciation and communication, not a full definition of the term.

The packet does not define “bilingual education” as an educational setting where children learn and communicate in two languages, nor does it explicitly state that the two languages are “typically their first language and a second language.”

While the packet supports that children’s L2 pronunciation patterns that differ from L1 speakers can affect communication effectiveness in bilingual education, the requested definition includes additional claims (the general definition/structure of bilingual education) that are not supported by the packet.
